intended_object: The subset relation s ⊆ t on subsets of a type α: every element of s is an element of t. The docstring and name say so.
explanation: The body is `∀ ⦃a⦄, a ∈ s₁ → a ∈ s₂`, which is the textbook definition of s₁ ⊆ s₂. It works for sets in any type α (any universe), which is the natural generality. The strict-implicit binder only changes how arguments are elaborated, not what the relation means. This is Mathlib's own basic definition, which the `HasSubset (Set α)` instance (the `⊆` notation) is built on. So the only other related declaration is the generic notation class `HasSubset.Subset`, which is not a separate definition of subset for sets. Degenerate cases behave correctly: the empty set is a subset of every set, and every set is a subset of itself.
